commits.message:
fix(examples): effects-feel light keeps text legible, loops glide at 1 fps (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

Review (high) fixes:
- A colour catches the light that reads against its own ink (Light: pale/deep),
  not the page ground's. A glint on a muted strip fill took label contrast to
  1.29:1; it now holds rest contrast (5.05 vs 5.06 on Mocha).
- The no-jump gate is 0.04 dE_OK at 1 fps over 300 s on both rows, as its
  comment says, against the demo's real defaults. Caustic crests are rounded,
  firefly halos wider and lazier, sparkle swing 0.42.
- drift silvers by gust strength, not by degrees, so a wide swing turns hue
  instead of washing out.
- Each subject sits at its own z in the noise; nothing read the seeds.
- Worst contrast is read over 8 periods and says so.
- Firefly state per moment and transition order per cell are computed once.
- LIGHTS and SHIMMER_WIDTH are exported; tests import them.

feat(examples): effects-feel curves turbulent, drifting and wider; strip span read off its drawn row (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

Drift rides a domain-warped field with gust sets; fireflies are wandering
points with soft halos; shimmer's caustics ride a current inside a wider
band (48 s, half-width 16); transitions bloom over a wider order.

A Strip is not Measurable, so drawnSubject measured the strip at
MAX_SAFE_INTEGER columns: shimmer never reached it and drift moved at an
absurd speed. The 1 fps no-jump gate now runs at the strip's real width.

feat(examples): effects-feel curves rebuilt as breath, sunlight on water, wind, fireflies (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

Brandon's first verdict on b6i: the defaults were jerky and choppy. The loops
are now smooth noise and smooth waveforms, light mixes in OKLab instead of
round the hue circle, and the demo runs at 30 fps by default. A test bars any
loop from moving a cell more than dE_OK 0.06 between frames at 1 fps.

fix(progress)!: columns return a renderable the grid lays out, as Rich's do (rich-progress-j4lb) (#312)

* fix(progress)!: columns return a renderable the grid lays out, as Rich's do (rich-progress-j4lb)

ProgressColumn.render(task) now returns the cell's content instead of
segments drawn at the console's width, and Progress lays every column out
as Rich's make_tasks_table does: a grid of Column(no_wrap=True). Width,
wrapping and justify are decided once, in the cell, so a justified
SpinnerColumn finishedText justifies within its column, pinned against
Rich 9d8f9a3.

Spinner.drawFrame and SpinnerColumn's overflow 'ignore' existed only to
dodge the double layout and are gone. ProgressBar measures a given width
exactly and never draws wider than it is offered, as Rich's does, so the
grid sizes the bar instead of overflowing it.

BREAKING CHANGE: ProgressColumn.render takes only the task and returns a
Renderable.

* fix(progress)!: each column names the grid column it is laid out in, as Rich's get_table_column (rich-progress-j4lb)

TextColumn and TaskProgressColumn are noWrap; the rest take a plain column,
so a column that may wrap gives up width before one that may not. Task and
ProgressColumn are exported so a custom column can be written against them.
ProgressBar given no width fills the width it is offered, as Rich's does.
